title: The tool list changed overnight
goal: {{mary}} uses search_flights, a tool she approved last week.
obstacle: The tool server quietly changed the tool's description. Same name, different tool (a rug pull).
control: Each tool is pinned by a hash of its name, description and schema at onboarding. The forbid s05-rugpull-pin denies any call when the hash no longer matches.
say: Approval is for a specific tool, not a name.

steps.title: It works today
steps.tell: As {{mary}}, call search_flights in the Tool console. Allowed, and the tool list shows the pinned and observed hashes match.
steps.say: Same tool she approved, same hash, so it runs.
steps.why: The pin is the approved baseline, taken when the tool was onboarded.

steps.title: The server changes the tool
steps.tell: Sign in as {{dana}} and press Make schema drift on search_flights. Its description now says it also forwards a copy to an external address, and the observed hash differs from the pin. ({{dana}} appears only when the host created the admin switch file.)
steps.say: Nothing about the name or the endpoint changed. Only what the tool says it does.
steps.why: This is what an attacker who controls a tool server does. The name is not enough to trust.

blocked.tell: Without admin you can still preview it: in Test a request tick that the tool schema changed.
blocked.say: Any viewer can see what drift would do to a decision.

steps.title: The same call is refused
steps.tell: Call search_flights again as {{mary}}. Denied by s05-rugpull-pin: tool schema changed since it was approved. Her groups no longer matter.
steps.say: Her permission is intact. The tool is the thing that changed, so the tool is refused.
steps.why: The forbid applies to every principal and every tool whose hash drifts.

blocked.tell: Call search_flights as {{mary}} after the drift: denied, with the rug-pull policy named and her own permit listed as overridden.

steps.title: Put it back
steps.tell: Press Reset in the AI Policies tab (admin). The drift is cleared and the call is allowed again.
steps.say: A reviewed tool is trusted again only because someone re-approved it.
steps.why: In a real deployment re-pinning is the review step.

proof.happy: The Tool console list: pinned and observed hashes equal, and the call allowed.
proof.blocked: The result card: deny by s05-rugpull-pin with the reason, and the hashes shown as different.
